newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Two Colombian cities rocked by bomb blasts.
newsitem.headline: Two Colombian cities rocked by bomb blasts.

text.p: Two Colombian cities, including the capital, were shaken by bomb blasts early on Thursday, but only one person was reported injured, authorities said.

Two of the bombs exploded outside betting parlours in the northwest city of Medellin, one of them located in the city's main bus terminal, police said. A third, consisting of about 22 pounds (10 kg) of dynamite, exploded in a commercial area on the south end of Bogota where one man was injured and windows were shattered in a block-long area.

There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the bombings, which occurred as Congress was debating legislation that would stiffen penalities for drug trafficking and lift Colombia's controversial ban on extradition.

Drug traffickers led by Pablo Escobar, the late and notoriously violent Medellin cartel kingpin, waged a bloody campaign of bombings, kidnappings and assassinations against extradition in the late 1980s and early 1990s.
